title: Skint Dave from Barnsley
story: A warm northern character anthem about daily struggles, ADHD weather, leaking washing machines, hearing aids, and the stubborn spirit of Dave from Barnsley refusing to give in.

lyrics.text: Morning sticks to the curtains, kettle takes its time
Fester guards the toolbox, Ralf is stealing mine
Nic says, “You’ve got a plan then?” I say, “I’ve got a few”
There’s a chair that needs repairing and a shed that wants me too
My left side’s playing hide-and-seek
The batteries chirp when I try to speak
The room keeps ringing like a shop alarm
Still I pull my boots on, still I mean no harm
I’m skint, Dave from Barnsley, counting pennies by the sink
Body coming loose at the seams, but I’m not done, I think
Fester, Ralf and Nic keep pulling me through
Every daft little project is a road I can choose
If the day says no, I’ll have another go
There’s a small light somewhere and I’m learning where it goes
Ramsey Hunt left a calling card beside my tired eye
Hearing aid whistles back whenever buses pass me by
Tinnitus fills the quiet, sleep forgets my name
I wake up feeling ninety, then I try the game again
The washing machine is leaking by the door
My knees have started arguing with the floor
Nic puts tea beside me, says, “Don’t make it grand”
So I draw another sketch with a pencil in my hand
I’m skint, Dave from Barnsley, counting pennies by the sink
Body coming loose at the seams, but I’m not done, I think
Fester, Ralf and Nic keep pulling me through
Every daft little project is a road I can choose
If the day says no, I’ll have another go
There’s a small light somewhere and I’m learning where it goes
One plan for a planter, one plan for a shelf
Three half-built inventions scattered round myself
ADHD weather, thunder in my head
But Nic finds the missing screw beneath the bed
I turn the power on and something starts to hum
Not the ringing in my ears this time—something I have done
I’m skint, Dave from Barnsley, but the numbers start to change
That little thing I built today has found its way to someone’s place
Fester’s on the worktop, Ralf is curled up blue
Nic is laughing in the doorway saying, “See, I knew you’d do”
If the day says no, I’ll have another go
There’s a small light getting brighter and I’m learning where it goes
The kettle clicks, the morning comes, the workshop catches fire
Not a blaze, just one good idea climbing a little higher
I’m still here, still trying, with a spark beneath the skin
Skint, Dave from Barnsley—and tonight, I think I win

title: Penny, You're Still Here
story: An uplifting story of overcoming addiction and generational hardship in Barnsley, finding strength through family love for 11-year-old Riley and 2-year-old Tommy.

lyrics.text: Penny grew up where the coal dust stayed,
Barnsley rain on the windowpane.
Jamie was older, trying to stand tall,
Chelsea was little, afraid of it all.
She learned to smile when the cupboard was bare,
To hide heavy thoughts beneath brushed hair.
Some nights the bottle promised relief,
Then morning came carrying shame and grief.
But underneath the hurt, underneath the years,
A small brave voice was louder than fear.
Penny, you're still here, still breathing,
Still got a heart that won't stop beating.
Riley needs your arms, Tommy needs your light,
There's a road out of the longest night.
Step by step, with the past behind,
You can leave those chains, you can change your mind.
Penny, the world can be kind again,
This is where your new life begins.
Eleven-year-old Riley watched her face,
Two-year-old Tommy reached for her embrace.
She saw in their eyes what she couldn't deny,
A reason to rise, a reason to try.
Jamie called round, and Chelsea came too,
No grand words, just a hand held true.
The old days pulled like a river in flood,
But Penny kept choosing the people she loved.
There were tears on the kitchen floor,
But she didn't sleep there anymore.
Penny, you're still here, still breathing,
Still got a heart that won't stop beating.
Riley needs your arms, Tommy needs your light,
There's a road out of the longest night.
Step by step, with the past behind,
You can leave those chains, you can change your mind.
Penny, the world can be kind again,
This is where your new life begins.
One honest morning, one open door,
One promise stronger than before.
David stood beside her, steady and true,
And Penny found the strength to follow through.
No miracle erased what had been,
Just courage to begin again.
Penny, you're still here, still believing,
Still got a heart that won't stop beating.
Riley's laughing, Tommy's holding tight,
The kitchen's full of ordinary light.
Jamie and Chelsea see her stand,
A brighter future built by hand.
Penny, the world is kind again,
This is where your new life begins.
From Barnsley rain to a clearer sky,
She chose tomorrow, she chose to try.
Penny, keep walking, the worst has passed,
A hard-won joy can last.

title: Dave from Barnsley
story: The legendary original UK comedy rap take on Dave, arguing with kettles, dealing with Ramsey Hunt and tinnitus, while cats Fester and Ralf prowl for breakfast.

lyrics.text: Yeah, this is Dave from Barnsley
Skint, knackered, still standing
Nic says, “You’ll get there”
The cats say nothing, they just want dinner
Wakes up grumpy, argues with the kettle
Bills on the table, nerves on the metal
One sock missing, toast burnt black
Fester wants breakfast, Ralf wants that
Nic says, “Breathe, love, take it slow”
Dave says, “I would, but me body says no”
Hearing aid squeals like a bus in a tunnel
Tinnitus drums on a permanent funnel
Ramsey Hunt left him feeling worn and strange
Still he checks the post for a life-changing change
Oh Dave, Dave, world’s most miserable man
Down on his luck but he’s doing what he can
With a head full of plans and a pocket full of lint
He keeps on trying though the battery’s spent
Oh Dave, Dave, don’t throw in the towel
Fester and Ralf are prowling for chow
Nic says, “One more go, you’re closer than you think”
He’s got one little spark, and it’s starting to blink
Project number one: fix the old machine
Project number two: build a better dream
Project number three: sell a clever guide
Project number four: the wheels fall off inside
ADHD brain does a lap of the room
Starts with a hammer, ends up painting the loo
Exhausted by breakfast, asleep by half ten
Wakes up annoyed, then he tries again
Back aches, knees creak, shoulder says “Why?”
He blames every joint on the weather outside
Nic brings tea and gives him the look
Fester steals a cable, Ralf eats the book
Oh Dave, Dave, world’s most miserable man
Down on his luck but he’s doing what he can
With a head full of plans and a pocket full of lint
He keeps on trying though the battery’s spent
Oh Dave, Dave, don’t throw in the towel
Fester and Ralf are prowling for chow
Nic says, “One more go, you’re closer than you think”
He’s got one little spark, and it’s starting to blink
Come on, Dave, get up, have another try
I’ve got a list, though I’ve lost where I put it
A half-built thing and a cat that’s chewed it
The world says no, but I’m not done yet
I’ve survived worse than a dodgy internet set
No grand parade, no miracle plan
Just one more step from a stubborn old man
If success is a door, I’ll lean on the frame
If it won’t open today, I’ll remember the name
Then one small customer says, “This works for me”
One proper payment, not a maybe or “we’ll see”
Dave checks the screen, then checks it again
Nic starts laughing, he nearly falls off the chair then
Fester looks proud, Ralf knocks over the light
The room’s still a mess, but the feeling is right
His body still groans and the ringing stays loud
But Dave lifts his chin and he’s grinning now
From Barnsley gloom to a modest success
Not fixed, not rich, but a little less stressed
Oh Dave, Dave, world’s most miserable man
Down on his luck but he’s doing what he can
With a head full of plans and a pocket of grit
He kept on moving and he’s landed a hit
Oh Dave, Dave, let the whole room know
Fester and Ralf, it’s time for the show
Nic says, “See? You’re closer than you think”
That little spark caught fire, now it’s starting to link
Still grumpy, still tired, still losing his pen
Still starting new projects at quarter past ten
But the kettle is singing, the cats have been fed
And Dave’s got a future inside his head
One small win, one stubborn man
Barnsley’s finest doing what he can

title: Crazy Rap
story: A high-octane council estate comedy rap filled with puns about mud, Sharon in wellies, Kev doing deals by the bins, and tea in the mug.

lyrics.text: Oi, mind the puddle by the stairwell
Kettle on, telly loud
Woke up to a council letter stuck to the door,
Said the rent needs sorting — I’ve heard that before.
Down by the bins, Kev’s doing deals with a grin,
While Sharon in wellies brings the mud right in.
She’s a proper muck magnet, boots full of clay,
Says, “Come on, handsome, let’s get filthy today.”
I said, “Love, I’ve got manners, a mop and a plan,”
She said, “Forget the mop — be a mucky woman’s man.”
Tea in the mug, green in the tin,
Neighbours start knocking: “Can we come in?”
One little laugh turns the whole block mad,
Best worst evening that we’ve ever had.
Crazy rap from the flats, no lift, just stairs,
Mud on the mat and smoke in the airs.
Mucky woman dancing like she owns the hall,
Puns so rude make the plaster fall.
Crazy rap, let the whole block sing,
Council-estate royalty, plastic-gold ring.
If life gets grim, we make it slap,
Put the kettle on — it’s the crazy rap!
She said, “You’re a grass,” I said, “No, I’m a sage,”
She said, “That’s not a herb, that’s a landlord’s rage.”
Got a spliff in the garden, but the garden’s a tray,
Three dead plants and a fox that won’t go away.
Her coat’s second-hand but her attitude’s new,
Got mud on her leggings and a point of view.
She called me a stud — I said, “That’s a screw,”
Now I’m fixing the cupboard while she fixes my mood.
Bangers in the kitchen, bass through the wall,
Someone’s burnt the toast, but we’re blaming the hall.
The dog’s got my slipper, the cat’s got the cap,
Everybody’s skanking to the crazy rap.
Crazy rap from the flats, no lift, just stairs,
Mud on the mat and smoke in the airs.
Mucky woman dancing like she owns the hall,
Puns so rude make the plaster fall.
Crazy rap, let the whole block sing,
Council-estate royalty, plastic-gold ring.
If life gets grim, we make it slap,
Put the kettle on — it’s the crazy rap!
She said, “Call me dirty,” I said, “That’s your brand,”
She slipped in the puddle and still took my hand.
We laughed so hard that the neighbours complained,
Then borrowed our sugar and came back again.
No palace, no marble, no chandelier,
Just love by the launderette and a bargain-bin beer.
Crazy rap from the flats, no lift, just stairs,
Mud on the mat and smoke in the airs.
Mucky woman dancing like she owns the hall,
Puns so rude make the plaster fall.
Crazy rap, let the whole block sing,
Council-estate royalty, plastic-gold ring.
If life gets grim, we make it slap,
Put the kettle on — it’s the crazy rap!
Mind the step, mind the mop,
Mind that woman — she don’t stop.
Green in the tin, tea in the cup,
Estate life down, but the chorus up.

title: Statistically, We're Fine
story: Dry British deadpan comedy hip-hop about velvet waistcoats, spreadsheets for feelings, emergency stair whistles, and orderly panic.

lyrics.text: Right—keep it tidy.
No, actually, don’t.
I bought a velvet waistcoat from a man called Dave,
He said, “It’s nearly vintage,” I said, “Nearly’s brave.”
Got a spreadsheet for my feelings, colour-coded in despair,
And a tiny little whistle for emergencies involving stairs.
I’m remarkably composed in a queue for a kebab,
Till a pigeon stole my napkin and I called it a cab.
I’ve got manners like a butler, taste buds like a bin,
Put a crown upon a sausage and I’ll probably let it in.
Hold up—
What was that?
No, leave it.
That’s definitely part of the plan.
We’re doing fine, we’re doing fine,
Absolutely normal, every single time.
Hands up high if your life’s off-line,
We’re doing fine, we’re doing fine.
Say, “Fine!”
(Fine!)
Say, “Fine!”
(Fine!)
That’s the spirit—statistically, we’re fine.
I rehearsed an apology in case I bump a chair,
Then I blamed the architecture with a confident stare.
My neighbour owns a parrot that has learned to swear,
Now it’s more emotionally available than anyone upstairs.
I made a five-year plan, it lasted till Tuesday,
Bought a motivational mug, it said, “Try again someday.”
My barber asked for guidance; I said, “Surprise me, mate,”
Now I look like a haunted pear that’s running late.
The bass drops out—
The room gets tense—
I’ve got one thought
And it’s making no sense.
I’m fluent in excuses, conversational in cheek,
I can turn a minor setback to a documentary critique.
Got a sandwich in my pocket and a theory in my shoe,
If confidence was currency, I’d owe a pound or two.
You can call me unrealistic; I prefer “future-famous,”
I put “enigmatic” on a form that asked for “name and address.”
When the punchline lands sideways, let the brass section shout,
If you didn’t get the first one, there’s another one—watch out.
We’re doing fine, we’re doing fine,
Absolutely normal, every single time.
Hands up high if your life’s off-line,
We’re doing fine, we’re doing fine.
Say, “Fine!”
(Fine!)
Say, “Fine!”
(Fine!)
That’s the spirit—statistically, we’re fine.
No further questions.
Please form an orderly panic.
We’re doing fine.
